head.name: @fzlt/core/layout
head.lead: Force-directed layout on typed arrays, with a Barnes-Hut pass, for diagrams and graphs that settle. Nodes repel (a quadtree, rebuilt each step, sums far groups as one mass: O(n log n)), links pull like springs toward their length, and a weak pull holds the graph around (cx, cy). One tick per fixed step, so a run replays exactly. - Settle: alpha cools from 1 toward 0 over ticks steps; when it is spent, or nothing moved more than still px in a step, the layout rests and stops calling busy(): the engine sleeps. heat(), pin() and link() warm it up and wake the engine. - Reduced motion: the whole run happens in one step, so the graph lands where it settles. - Zero allocation per step; fixed capacity (cap nodes, links links: add and link return -1 when full). - DOM-free: draw it anywhere (@fzlt/core/view-canvas), frame it with @fzlt/core/camera (bounds). Distances use steer's exact hypot (Math.hypot boxes its arguments).

sizesNote: Measured on this build: minified and gzipped with everything it imports, the way npm run size checks the budget in CI.

blocks.code:
const g = layout(e, { cap: 64, cx: 320, cy: 200 }); // DOM-free, typed arrays
const a = g.add(), b = g.add();
g.link(a, b, 60); // settles in ≤ 300 steps, then stops calling busy()
g.pin(a, px, py); // a drag: the rest flows round it; g.free(a) lets go
const [l, t, r, b] = g.bounds(box); // left, top, right, bottom
fit(cam, l, t, r - l, b - t); // frame it with @fzlt/core/camera
